patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Dorothy Harrington is a 74-year-old right-handed woman with a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diet-controlled type 2 diabetes who was brought to the emergency department by her daughter after sudden onset of left-sided weakness and behavioral change. The daughter reports she called her mother at approximately 09:00 this morning and she sounded entirely normal. She arrived at her mother's home at 11:20 for a planned visit and found her sitting in the kitchen chair unable to rise, with her left arm hanging limply at her side and appearing oblivious to objects and people on her left side. The patient denied anything was wrong when asked, attributing her inability to stand to her bad knees. The daughter called 911 immediately. EMS arrived at 11:34 and documented left hemiplegia, apparent neglect of the left side, and rightward gaze preference. A stroke alert was activated in the field. Blood glucose obtained by EMS was 128 mg/dL. The patient arrived in the emergency department at 11:58. Last known well time is established at 09:00, approximately 2 hours and 58 minutes before ED arrival, placing her within the standard IV alteplase window. On cardiac monitoring in the ED, the rhythm appeared irregularly irregular, prompting an urgent 12-lead ECG. The patient is unable to reliably report symptom onset; she demonstrates apparent anosognosia for her left-sided deficits. She denies headache, nausea, vomiting, or loss of consciousness. She reports no recent chest pain, fever, or illness. Her medications include amlodipine, lisinopril, atorvastatin, and aspirin 81 mg daily. She has not taken any anticoagulants. Her blood pressure on arrival is 188/104 mmHg, which she and her daughter attribute to her chronic hypertension. The daughter confirms her mother has never been diagnosed with atrial fibrillation and has not seen a cardiologist in several years.
